analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-buffer-overflow is caused by missing register-bound checks in VM opcode handlers that index the current stack frame via untrusted bytecode operand `a`. In this PoV, execution reaches OP_SETIDX and unconditionally writes `SET_NIL_VALUE(regs[a+3])`; when `a` is crafted near the end of the allocated stack frame, this writes past `c->stend` (ASan shows write at exactly end of 1024-byte stack buffer). The root cause is unsafe use of `a`-based register offsets in `mrb_vm_exec` without validating that `a+N < irep->nregs` / current frame capacity before read/write.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: `mruby_fuzzer` calls `mrb_load_string` on attacker-controlled bytes, compiler/parser produces an irep, then `mrb_vm_run` initializes a fixed initial stack (128 mrb_value) and calls `mrb_vm_exec`. A malformed script/bytecode sequence must drive VM to an opcode path using multi-slot register access (here OP_SETIDX with `regs[a+3]`) with an out-of-range `a` value relative to available registers/stack. Because no bounds check is done before the write, a heap OOB write occurs.
